title: Spiralized Beet Noodles: Colorful Side Dish for Thanksgiving
meta_description: Discover how to make vibrant spiralized beet noodles for Thanksgiving. Learn step‑by‑step tips, seasoning ideas, and how the Vegetable Spiralizer makes it effor
html:
Spiralized beet noodles add a burst of color and earthy sweetness to your Thanksgiving table, and they’re surprisingly easy to prepare. Using a good vegetable spiralizer, you can turn raw beets into bright, noodle‑like ribbons that hold up well in a warm side dish or a chilled salad. Below you’ll find a practical workflow, flavor‑pairing suggestions, and storage tips so the beet noodles stay crisp and vivid through the holiday rush.

Why Spiralized Beet Noodles Belong on Your Thanksgiving Menu

Beets bring a natural ruby hue that contrasts beautifully with traditional turkey gravy and creamy mashed potatoes. When you spiralize them, the texture mimics pasta while staying low‑carb and nutrient‑dense. The natural sweetness of beets pairs well with tangy vinaigrette, roasted nuts, or a drizzle of citrus‑infused olive oil—making them a versatile side that can be served hot or cold.

Choosing the Right Beet and Getting It Ready

Pick beets that are firm, smooth, and free of cracks. Smaller to medium‑sized beets are easier to handle on a handheld or countertop spiralizer. After washing, peel the skins with a vegetable peeler or paring knife; the skins can add bitterness if left on. Trim the ends, then slice the beet into 2‑inch lengths that fit comfortably into the spiralizer’s feed tube.

Spiralizing Beet Noodles with the Vegetable Spiralizer

The Vegetable Spiralizer works whether you prefer a compact handheld model for quick prep or a larger countertop version for batch cooking. Here’s a quick run‑through:

  1. Secure the beet piece on the feed tube and turn the crank (handheld) or push the lever (countertop) to feed it through.
  2. Adjust the blade selector to the desired thickness—medium strands give the best bite for a side dish.
  3. Collect the ribbons in a bowl; they will release a little moisture as they spin.
  4. Rinse the noodles briefly in cold water to stop any residual cooking and pat dry with a clean kitchen towel.

Because beets are dense, you may need to apply a little pressure, but the spiralizer’s sturdy design handles it without jamming.

Flavor‑Building: Dressing, Crunch, and Warm‑Up Options

Once you have your spiralized beet noodles, think about the flavor profile you want. Here are three tried‑and‑true combinations that shine at Thanksgiving:

  • Maple‑Dijon Vinaigrette: Whisk together 2 Tbsp maple syrup, 1 Tbsp Dijon mustard, 1 Tbsp apple cider vinegar, ¼ cup extra‑virgin olive oil, and a pinch of sea salt. Toss the noodles and let them sit for 10 minutes to absorb the glaze.
  • Roasted Walnut & Sage: Toast ½ cup walnut halves with 1 tsp fresh sage leaves in a dry skillet until fragrant. Sprinkle over the noodles with a drizzle of lemon‑infused olive oil for crunch and aroma.
  • Warm Garlic‑Butter Sauté: Melt 2 Tbsp butter in a skillet, add 2 minced garlic cloves, and sauté the beet noodles for 2‑3 minutes until just tender. Finish with a squeeze of orange juice and a sprinkle of grated pecorino.

All three options keep the beet’s natural color vivid while adding complementary textures and flavors.

Serving Tips and Storage for Thanksgiving Day

To keep the noodles from turning mushy, serve them either immediately or store them in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. If you need to reheat, do so gently in a skillet with a splash of broth; over‑cooking will cause the beet strands to lose their snap. For a cold presentation, keep the noodles on a chilled platter and drizzle the dressing just before guests arrive.

FAQ

Can I use other vegetables with the same recipe?

Absolutely. Spiralized carrots, sweet potatoes, or even a mix of beets and zucchini work well. Adjust the cooking time slightly for each vegetable’s density.

Do I need to blanch the beet noodles before dressing them?

No blanching is required. The beet’s natural moisture is enough to let the vinaigrette cling, and a brief sauté will warm them without losing texture.

Is the Vegetable Spiralizer dishwasher safe?

Most models are top‑rack dishwasher‑safe, but hand‑washing the blade and feed tube prolongs sharpness and prevents rust.
